name: Green academia

lead: Green academia is one of several "academia" aesthetics that grew out of dark academia, an internet style based on idealised higher education, literature and the arts. Green academia leans on nature, with greens and earthy tones in classic scholarly clothing.
People use it as a wardrobe framework: cardigans, blazers, tweed and dress shirts in a consistent palette create a put-together look.

paras: Dark academia clothing draws on 1930s and 1940s Oxbridge and Ivy League fashion: cardigans, blazers, dress shirts, plaid, Oxford shoes, houndstooth and tweed, in a palette that already includes dark green. Green academia shifts the emphasis toward greens and nature imagery.
Minimal; the main cost is clothing.

angle.text: The aesthetic provides a consistent wardrobe theme, so clothes work together and the outfit looks deliberate.

lead: Green academia is an internet aesthetic in the academia family. Wikipedia lists it, with gothic and chaotic academia, as a related style to dark academia, the literary aesthetic centred on idealised higher education, arts and literature [1].

People use it to dress with a coherent theme: dark academia pieces such as cardigans, blazers, dress shirts, plaid and tweed, in palettes that already feature dark green [1]. Dark academia emerged on Tumblr around 2014 to 2015, spread to Instagram and Pinterest around 2017 and grew during the COVID-19 pandemic [1].
Beyond that listing, little published material describes green academia specifically.

paras: Dark academia clothing borrows from 1930s and 1940s fashion associated with Oxbridge, Ivy League and prep schools, with houndstooth and tweed, and a palette of black, white, beige, brown and dark green [1]. Light academia emerged partly in reaction with softer colours [1].
